LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: School Suggested vocabulary bell, lesson, chalkboard, chalk, books, block, bag, 
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of School Suggested vocabulary bell, lesson, chalkboard, chalk, books, block, bag,  in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to listen attentively when other people are talking?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to audio-visual recordings of songs, a story, teacher read aloud stories, among others, with the target letter –sound combination.

2. pick words with the target letter – sound combination - bl as in blue, - sp as in spoon, - sc as in school, - sk as in sky - ck –as in kick

3. practice using the target letter-sound combinations to form words.

4. construct simple sentences using new words,

5. listen and respond to two- directional instructions without interrupting as modeled by the teacher or peers.

6. In groups, learners are guided to develop a talking tree using the new words, learners with low vision to write on manila cards and learners with blindness to write the new words on braille cards. 1)

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to audio-visual recordings of songs, a story, teacher read aloud stories, among others, with the target letter –sound combination.
2. pick words with the target letter – sound combination - bl as in blue, - sp as in spoon, - sc as in school, - sk as in sky - ck –as in kick
3. practice using the target letter-sound combinations to form words.
4. construct simple sentences using new words,
5. listen and respond to two- directional instructions without interrupting as modeled by the teacher or peers.
6. In groups, learners are guided to develop a talking tree using the new words, learners with low vision to write on manila cards and learners with blindness to write the new words on braille cards. 1)

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: A learner applies the knowledge of letter sounds and syllables to identify words with target letter sounds.

● Communication and collaboration: A learner works in groups to practice using the target letter-sound combinations.

● Self-Efficacy: A learner’s self-esteem is nurtured as they learn to pronounce words correctly in communication.

Values:
Respect is enhanced as a learner appreciates diverse opinions of peers during group activities.

PCIs: Life-skill (self-awareness) the learner self-awareness is enhanced as they name the things found in the school environment.

Link to other Learning Areas:

• This applies attentive listening skills to the learning of concepts to the other learning areas.
